finding.claim: StartActionByGet and StartActionByGetAndWait never call validateJustificationRequired, and the executor does not enforce it either. Any caller with exec permission can run an action that is configured to require a justification, without giving one.
finding.source: Unauthenticated or low-privilege caller (a guest if guests have exec permission) sends StartActionByGet or StartActionByGetAndWait with only an action_id. Precondition: the action requires justification and has no mandatory arguments.
finding.sink: executor.ExecRequest runs the action with an empty justification.

trace.note: StartAction calls validateJustificationRequired before running the action
StartActionByGet builds the ExecutionRequest directly, with no justification resolution or validation
StartActionByGetAndWait follows the same path through startActionByGetAndWaitLogEntry and runBindingAndWait (api.go:345-358), also with no justification check
ResolveJustification only fills in a default for system users. For a normal user it returns "" and does not fail
The justification is only recorded on the log entry. No chain step rejects an empty one

finding.guards_checked: stepACLCheck still applies, so exec permission is needed. I grepped the executor for a justification-required enforcement step and found none. Only the StartAction and StartActionAndWait handlers check it.

finding.claim: checkUserFromHeaders copies a client-controlled `provider` request header into AuthenticatedUser.Provider. A client can send `provider: system` and be treated as a system execution, which satisfies the justification requirement. The `provider` header is also not part of the configured trusted username/usergroup headers, so a reverse proxy will not strip it.
finding.source: HTTP request header `provider` sent by any client. Precondition: authHttpHeaderUsername is configured, so the header-auth user is non-empty and the chain returns it.
finding.sink: IsSystemExecution (executor/justification.go:26) and justificationProvided (api_justification.go:30-32) skip the justification requirement. Provider is also used for session and logout handling and for IsGuest.

trace.note: u.Provider = value of the request header named `provider`
The header user is returned first in the chain when Username != "", with Provider kept as supplied
IsSystemExecution is true when Provider == "system" and Username != "guest"
justificationProvided returns true for system executions even when the justification is empty
validateJustificationRequired is bypassed on StartAction and StartActionAndWait

finding.guards_checked: The username header is trusted by design (proxy-set). Nothing sanitizes or strips the `provider` header, and nothing restricts Provider values for header-authenticated users.

finding.claim: The OAuth2 `state` value is used as the authenticated session ID. It is the olivetin-sid-oauth cookie value and the key in registeredStates, and it also appears in the authorize URL and the /oauth/callback?state=... URL. Anyone who learns the state, for example from proxy or IdP logs, Referer headers or browser history, can present it as the cookie and be authenticated as the user once the callback completes. The session ID is also fixed before login.
finding.source: State value exposed in URLs (the redirect to the provider and the callback query string), or planted in a victim's browser by cookie injection. Precondition: an OAuth2 provider is configured and the victim completes login while the state is still valid.
finding.sink: CheckUserFromOAuth2Cookie / lookupOAuth2UserByState returns the user (Username and Usergroup) identified by the state, and the API uses it for authorization.

trace.note: state = randString(16), generated before authentication
The state is set as the olivetin-sid-oauth cookie
The same state is sent in the AuthCodeURL redirect
On callback, the state entry is filled in with the Username and Usergroup
The cookie value is looked up directly as the session (lines 432-447), with no rotation after login

finding.guards_checked: The callback checks that the cookie matches the query state (line 190), which blocks a plain callback CSRF. The state is not regenerated after authentication. The cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax, but the value is also present in URLs.

finding.claim: GetEntities and GetEntity return entity data without checking whether the caller may view any related action. GetEntities returns every instance of every type, and GetEntity returns any instance by type and unique key. With no entity properties configured, all fields are dumped via serializeEntityFields. A caller with only dashboard access, including a guest when guests are not required to log in, can read entities that ACLs would otherwise hide.
finding.source: GetEntities and GetEntity RPC requests from any caller who passes checkDashboardAccess, including a guest. Preconditions: entity files are loaded and the entity data is sensitive.
finding.sink: buildEntityResponse, buildSortedEntityInstances and serializeEntityFields return entity Title, UniqueKey and Fields.

trace.note: The user is resolved, and only checkDashboardAccess is applied
entities.GetEntities() returns the unfiltered global map
All instances are built with no per-user filtering
GetEntity looks up instances by request type and key, and acl.IsAllowedView is not called
serializeEntityFields includes every field of the entity map when no properties are configured

finding.guards_checked: checkDashboardAccess only blocks guests when authRequireGuestsToLogin is set. There is no ACL check on entities. userCanViewAction is applied only to related actions (api_entity_related_actions.go:57).

finding.claim: The unauthenticated PasswordHash RPC uses the same 10-slot argon2 semaphore as local login. An attacker can keep the slots busy with PasswordHash requests so that legitimate LocalUserLogin calls get ErrArgon2Busy (CodeResourceExhausted). This is a denial of service on interactive login.
finding.source: Unauthenticated PasswordHash requests sent in a loop. No auth is required: the handler never calls UserFromApiCall.
finding.sink: argon2Sem in local_user_login.go, shared by CreateHash and comparePasswordAndHash.

trace.note: PasswordHash has no authentication or rate limit and calls createHash
CreateHash takes a slot from argon2Sem (capacity 10) and returns ErrArgon2Busy when full
comparePasswordAndHash uses the same semaphore
Login returns ResourceExhausted on ErrArgon2Busy

finding.guards_checked: The semaphore bounds memory use but also makes the shared slots an attacker-controlled resource. I found no per-IP or per-endpoint limits and no separate pool for hashing and login.
